r0.why: Definition, equivalence of units, surface energy being broader and applying to solids, and liquid usage all from [1]-[4].

r1.why: Cohesive force definition [15], zero net interior force [11], inward pull at surface [12], contraction to minimum area [13], tension along surface resisting external force [14].

r2.why: Lower energy with neighbour [24], boundary molecules higher energy [25], minimising them [26], minimal area [27], smooth shape [28]; opening line is framing only.

r3.why: Shape of droplets [19], easily deformed but pulled spherical by cohesive imbalance [20], virtually all liquids spherical [21], minimum area for volume first noted by Gibbs [44].

r4.why: Hydrogen-bond web and 72.8 mN/m at 20 C [6], denser objects like razor blades and water striders float without partial submersion [7], surfactants such as detergents reduce it for more contact [9].

r5.why: Adhesive forces between different molecules [15] and container [16], balance sets wetting/contact angle/meniscus [16], mercury convex low wetting [17], water concave high wetting [18].
